decisive_spans.text: An 80-year-old Japanese woman with no smoking history was referred to respiratory medicine for dyspnea on exertion. Seven years prior, she was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian serous adenocarcinoma and received TC chemotherapy followed by surgery. After 21 cycles of TC chemotherapy, she started maintenance therapy. She had no notable medical or family history except for ovarian cancer.
Diffuse ground-glass opacity, mosaic attenuation, and ill-defined centrilobular nodules
Krebs von den Lungen-6 level: 1250 U/mL

response.rationale: The patient's history of TC chemotherapy, dyspnea on exertion, diffuse ground-glass opacity, mosaic attenuation, and ill-defined centrilobular nodules, along with an elevated Krebs von den Lungen-6 level, strongly support drug-induced pneumonitis. The absence of other significant medical history further points to this diagnosis. While D3 (Drug-Induced Interstitial Lung Disease) is similar, D4 is more specific and includes the elevated Krebs von den Lungen-6 level as a support item.
